## Welcome {.unnumbered}

This past week, you worked on your first Quarto document. You created the file,
put your name in the header, added a code chunk and rendered it to HTML. 

This warm-up four short parts. At each one, **commit to an answer before you open
the reveal**. Say it out loud to your neighbour before you open the reveal. 


## Stop 1. Anatomy of a `.qmd` file {.unnumbered}

[≈ 2 minutes]{.timing}

Here is a complete Quarto document, like the one you made last week:

````markdown
---
title: "My First Quarto Document"
author: "Ana Smith"
format: html
---

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button, a document will be generated.

```{{r}}
1 + 1
```
````

::: {.turn}
**Your turn.** This file has **three** kinds of content. Name each one and say
where it starts and ends. Then answer: which part is the *only* one R runs?
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Reveal

1. **The YAML header**, between the two `---` lines. It holds settings for the
   whole document: title, author and output format. Quarto reads it; R never
   does.
2. **Markdown text**: everything outside the header and the chunks. `##` makes
   a section heading and `**Render**` makes bold text. It's written for
   humans.
3. **A code chunk**, from the ` ```{r} ` line to the closing ` ``` `. **This is
   the only part R runs.** When you render, R runs the code and pastes the
   output into the document right below it.
:::

## Stop 2. Fix the header {.unnumbered}

[≈ 2 minutes]{.timing}

A pair wrote this header, clicked **Render**, and got an error instead of a
document:

````markdown
---
title: Pair Programming 2: Quarto in R
author Ana Smith
format: html

## Adding a Code Chunk
````

::: {.turn}
**Your turn.** There are **three** mistakes. Find all three before you open
the reveal.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Reveal

1. **The title has a colon in it and no quotes.** In YAML, a colon means
   "key: value", so a second colon confuses it. When a value contains a colon,
   put it in quotes.
2. **`author` is missing its colon.** Every line in the header is `key: value`.
3. **The header is never closed.** Without the second `---`, Quarto can't tell
   where the settings end and the document begins.

The fixed version:

````markdown
---
title: "Pair Programming 2: Quarto in R"
author: "Ana Smith"
format: html
---

## Adding a Code Chunk
````

**Good habit:** always put quotes around the title and author. They cost you
nothing and prevent the first mistake.
:::

## Stop 3. The code chunk {.unnumbered}

[≈ 3 minutes]{.timing}

Four students each tried to add a chunk that prints `"Hello, Quarto!"`:

::: {.chunk-grid}

**A**

````markdown
```{{r}}
print("Hello, Quarto!")
```
````

**B**

````markdown
```r
print("Hello, Quarto!")
```
````

**C**

````markdown
'''{r}
print("Hello, Quarto!")
'''
````

**D**

````markdown
```{{r}}
print("Hello, Quarto!")
````

:::

::: {.turn}
**Your turn.** Only one of these works. Which one? For each of the other three,
say what goes wrong.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Reveal

- **A works.** It has three backticks, `{r}` in curly braces, and three
  backticks to close it.
- **B has no curly braces.** Quarto shows the code as grey text but never runs
  it, so no `[1] "Hello, Quarto!"` appears below it. The `{ }` tells Quarto to
  run the code.
- **C uses apostrophes (`'''`), not backticks (` ``` `).** Quarto doesn't treat
  it as a chunk at all, so the three lines appear as ordinary text. The
  backtick key is at the top left of most keyboards, next to **1**.
- **D is never closed.** Quarto treats everything after it, to the end of the
  document, as part of the chunk. That usually causes an error, or swallows the
  rest of the document.

**Tip:** the green **+C** button in RStudio (or **Cmd+Option+I** on Mac,
**Ctrl+Alt+I** on Windows) inserts a correct chunk, so you never have to type
the fences.
:::

The grey box below is like the *inside* of a chunk. Whatever you type here is
exactly what you would put between ` ```{r} ` and ` ``` `.

::: {.turn}
**Your turn.** Make R print a greeting with **your own name** in it, e.g.
`"Hello, Ana!"`. Use `paste()` so that your name is stored in an object first.
:::

```{webr}
#| exercise: ex_hello
my_name <- "______"
______
```

::::: {.hint exercise="ex_hello"}
::: {.callout-tip collapse="false"}
## Hint

`paste()` glues pieces of text together, adding a space between them by
default. `paste0()` adds no space.

```r
paste("Hello,", "Quarto!")
```
:::
:::::

::: {.solution exercise="ex_hello"}
**Solution:**

```r
my_name <- "Ana"
paste0("Hello, ", my_name, "!")
```

Put these two lines inside a ` ```{r} ` chunk, render, and the rendered page
shows the code followed by `[1] "Hello, Ana!"`.
:::

## Stop 4. Predict the render {.unnumbered}

[≈ 2 minutes]{.timing}

::: {.turn}
**Your turn.** Imagine you click **Render** on the document from Stop 1. What
will the finished HTML page show, from top to bottom? Sketch it or describe it
before you open the reveal. In particular:

- Do the `---` lines appear on the page?
- Does the `##` appear?
- Does the page show `1 + 1`, `2`, or both?
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Reveal

Roughly this:

::: {.rendered}
<p class="r-title">My First Quarto Document</p>
<p class="r-meta">AUTHOR<br>Ana Smith</p>
<p class="r-h2">Running Code</p>
<p>When you click the <strong>Render</strong> button, a document will be generated.</p>
<pre class="r-code">1 + 1</pre>
<pre class="r-out">[1] 2</pre>
:::

- **The header disappears.** Its settings turn into the big title and the
  author line.
- **`##` disappears.** It becomes a section heading, and `**Render**` becomes
  **bold**.
- **You see both the code and its result.** By default Quarto shows the code
  *and* its output. The `[1]` just means "first element".
:::

## Last check {.unnumbered}

Answer these from memory, then open the reveal.

1. What's the keyboard shortcut for **Render**?
2. After rendering `analysis.qmd`, what new file appears, and where?
3. You fixed a typo but the rendered page still shows it. What's the most
   likely reason?

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Reveal

1. **Cmd+Shift+K** on Mac, **Ctrl+Shift+K** on Windows.
2. **`analysis.html`**, in the **same folder** as `analysis.qmd`. That HTML
   file is the one you share or submit. The `.qmd` is your source.
3. **You didn't re-render.** The HTML is a snapshot of the last render, and
   editing the `.qmd` doesn't change it until you click **Render** again.
   (RStudio saves the file when you render, but it's a good habit to save
   first anyway.)
:::

---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Why this matters:** your final project is a Quarto document, and the rubric
checks that it *renders cleanly*. Every mistake on this page is one you can now
spot in seconds.
:::
